previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary hyperaldosteronism, migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, obstructive sleep apnea, and hypertension was admitted for headache and hypertensive urgency with blood pressure up to 220/110. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or pulmonary process. Her headache persisted despite blood pressure control, and neurologic evaluation ruled out pseudotumor cerebri and hypertensive emergency, leading to a diagnosis of severe migraine. Blood pressure was managed with captopril initially, then transitioned to enalapril for better tolerability. Propranolol was reduced due to bradycardia, and tizanidine was discontinued due to QT prolongation risk. Headache improved with acetaminophen and short-term oxycodone. She was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up scheduled with neurology for ongoing headache management.
